purpose: Implements Critical CSS Generation — extracts and inlines above-the-fold CSS, defers full stylesheets via media="print" onload pattern, with per-template background processing (Action Scheduler), daily cron regeneration, and React admin UI with status panel.
riskRationale: Well-architected feature with heuristic extraction, background jobs, and clean React integration. Contains several fixable correctness bugs: a fatal-error namespace resolution issue, an overly-narrow catch clause that does not catch PHP 8.2+ Error types, a template-hash mismatch rendering custom page template CCSS non-functional, and unescaped CSS output that is a stored-XSS vector if the cache directory is compromised. No auth bypass or data exposure risks.
breakingChanges: New 'criticalCSS' setting key in file_optimisation options

text: Solid implementation of a complex performance feature. The heuristic CSS extraction, Action Scheduler background jobs, transient-based status tracking, and React UI integration are cleanly done. However, four critical correctness bugs (namespace-resolution fatal error, overly-narrow catch, template-hash mismatch for custom page templates, unescaped CSS output) and several important maintainability issues (hardcoded template list duplication, regex fragility, race condition, stuck-pending state) need resolution before merge. All fixes are straightforward with low regression risk.

reasoning: Four critical bugs exist: (1) namespace resolution causes fatal error in Cache::clear_ccss(), (2) catch (\Exception) misses PHP 8.2+ Error types, (3) get_current_template_slug() never returns custom page template slugs so generated CCSS is never served, (4) unescaped cache content inlined inside <style> is a stored-XSS vector. All are straightforward to fix.

message: Well-designed heuristic CSS extraction with brace-depth-based parser handling minified and multi-line CSS correctly. The token_match function uses word-boundary-aware matching to prevent false positives like .container matching .container-fluid.

First-visit trigger pattern: when no CCSS file exists, full stylesheets load normally and an Action Scheduler job is queued (deduplicated via as_next_scheduled_action). Subsequent visitors get the optimized page — correct progressive enhancement.

Defer stylesheet implementation handles media='all', media='screen', and absent media attributes with both quoting variants, includes a noscript fallback, and has an idempotency guard (data-wppo-ccss attribute) to prevent double-processing.

Clean React component with proper status-to-visual mapping via STATUS_CONFIG (ready/pending/failed/none), loading state on regenerate, error handling, and follows existing project patterns (FontAwesomeIcon, LoadingSubmitButton, BEM classes).
Good test coverage for the Critical CSS UI: switch rendering, conditional panel display, toggle show/hide behavior, regenerate button API call, and template label rendering.

Missing leading backslash in namespace-qualified static method call. Inside namespace PerformanceOptimise\Inc, the unqualified name PerformanceOptimise\Inc\Critical_CSS resolves to PerformanceOptimise\Inc\PerformanceOptimise\Inc\Critical_CSS, causing a PHP fatal error when clear_ccss() is invoked.
suggestion: Prefix the call with a leading backslash to make it an absolute namespace reference.

message: catch (\Exception $e) does not catch PHP 8.2+ Error subclasses (e.g., TypeError, ValueError). If CSSMinifier::minify() throws a non-Exception error, the exception propagates uncaught and crashes the page.
suggestion: Use \Throwable instead of \Exception to catch all error types.

message: get_current_template_slug() always returns 'page' for custom page templates (e.g., 'page-about.php'), but get_templates() includes custom templates via get_page_templates(). This creates a hash mismatch: CCSS generated for 'page-about.php' is stored under md5('page-about.php'.get_stylesheet()), but inline_ccss() looks up md5('page'.get_stylesheet()), so custom template CCSS is generated but never served.
suggestion: Update get_current_template_slug() to check get_page_template_slug() when is_page() is true, falling back to 'page' only if no custom template is set.

message: Unsanitized file content is echoed directly inside <style> tags. The phpcs:ignore comment asserts the content is safe because the plugin wrote it, but this is a user-writable cache directory. If any vulnerability allows writing to wp-content/cache/wppo/ccss/, an attacker can inject </style><script> for stored XSS.
suggestion: Sanitize the content by stripping HTML tags before echoing inside <style>.

message: Hardcoded template list ['index','home','single','page','archive'] in delete_all_cache_files() duplicates Critical_CSS::get_templates() and misses custom page templates. Their status transients are never cleared on cache clear, leading to stale UI state. The existing clear_ccss() method (line 949) correctly handles this by calling Critical_CSS::clear_all().
suggestion: Replace the duplicate template-transient clearing block with a call to self::clear_ccss() which delegates to Critical_CSS::clear_all().

message: regenerate_all() sets the status transient to 'pending' for ALL templates (line 1049) even when Action Scheduler is not available. The set_transient call is outside the if ( function_exists( 'as_enqueue_async_action' ) ) block, so when AS is unavailable, the UI shows 'pending' permanently with no background job ever scheduled.
suggestion: Move set_transient inside the Action Scheduler availability check, or add an else branch that sets status to 'failed'.

message: @font-face regex '/@font-face\s*\{[^}]+\}/is' uses [^}]+ which breaks on data URIs or CSS values containing nested braces (e.g., src: url(data:font/woff2;base64,...{...})). This truncates the @font-face block, causing FOIT. The same issue affects the :root and html CSS custom property regexes at lines 573 and 579.
suggestion: Use the brace-depth pattern already used for @keyframes extraction.

message: Race condition: the wppo_ccss_status_ transient is set to 'pending' AFTER as_enqueue_async_action() (line 900), but the as_next_scheduled_action() guard (line 894) only checks for pending/scheduled actions. In concurrent requests, both visitors can pass the guard before either sets the transient, causing duplicate generation jobs for the same template.
suggestion: Set the transient to 'pending' BEFORE enqueuing the action and check the transient as an additional guard.

message: Self-fetch recursion risk: generate() uses wp_remote_get() to fetch a page URL on the same site. Since inline_ccss() runs on wp_head, fetching the page triggers wp_head again, calling inline_ccss() recursively. If CCSS does not exist, each nested request enqueues another background job, creating cascading HTTP requests that can exhaust server resources — especially when multiple templates need generation simultaneously.
suggestion: Add a request flag (define or static property) that bypasses inline_ccss() and defer_stylesheets() during generation.

message: The generate() method has no check that DOMDocument or DOMXPath classes exist before instantiation. While the DOM extension is common, it is not guaranteed on all PHP installations. Missing DOM support would cause a fatal error.
suggestion: Add class_exists() checks before instantiating DOMDocument and DOMXPath, returning false gracefully if unavailable.

message: The DOMDocument encoding hack uses an invalid XML declaration: <?xml encoding="UTF-8"> is missing the closing ?>. Should be <?xml encoding="UTF-8"?>. While DOMDocument may parse this leniently, it is technically malformed and may produce warnings or mangled output with HTML5 elements like <picture> and <video>.
suggestion: Fix the XML declaration syntax.

message: All @supports, @layer, and @container blocks are included in critical CSS unconditionally without any above-fold selector filtering (lines 598-603). These blocks can be large, especially @layer from modern CSS frameworks, adding significant bloat to the inlined CSS without confirming the content is above-fold relevant.
suggestion: Parse the contents of @supports/@layer/@container blocks and apply the same above-fold selector filtering used in filter_media_query_rules().

message: No size limit on inlined critical CSS. Google recommends keeping critical CSS under ~14KB (at most 50KB) for mobile first paint. The entire extracted CSS (including @font-face, @keyframes, @supports blocks) is inlined unconditionally. A theme with many @font-face declarations could produce 100KB+ of inlined CSS, potentially making FCP/LCP worse.
suggestion: Add a configurable size cap (default ~50KB). If the generated CCSS exceeds the limit, truncate it and log a warning, or skip inlining.

message: fetch_stylesheet_with_imports() validates HTTP 200 but does not check the Content-Type header. If a URL returns an HTML error page served with a 200 status or a redirect that resolves to HTML, the content is treated as CSS, introducing malformed content into the extraction pipeline.
suggestion: After confirming 200 status, check that the Content-Type header contains 'text/css' or the URL ends with '.css' to skip non-CSS responses.

message: When Util::init_filesystem() returns false, generate_and_store() falls back to file_put_contents() directly, bypassing WordPress filesystem API. On many hosts, the web server user differs from the FTP/SSH user, so direct PHP file writes may fail or silently write to the wrong location with mismatched permissions.
suggestion: Remove the file_put_contents fallback and fail gracefully if WP_Filesystem cannot be initialized. Log the failure and set status to 'failed'.

message: Both minify_css (hooked at priority 10) and defer_stylesheets (hooked at priority 10) filter style_loader_tag with the same priority. When both minifyCSS and criticalCSS are enabled, execution order is fragile — any third-party plugin hooking at priority 10 could interact unpredictably.
suggestion: Run defer_stylesheets at a slightly higher priority (e.g., 9) so it always runs before minify_css.

message: The brace-depth parser in parse_regular_rules() does not account for braces inside CSS string values (e.g., background: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20%7B%7D%22)). A { or } inside a string literal would increment/decrement the brace depth incorrectly, causing the parser to lose sync with the actual rule structure.
suggestion: Track whether the parser is inside a string (single or double quotes) and skip brace counting inside string contexts.

message: Only max-width media queries are included in critical CSS. Desktop-critical layout rules wrapped in min-width queries are excluded, which could cause desktop visitors to experience FOUC or missing layout on wider viewports.
suggestion: Also include min-width media queries alongside the max-width extraction for balanced mobile-first and desktop coverage.

message: The @import regex does not handle media-qualified imports like @import url('style.css') screen; or @import 'style.css' screen and (min-width: 768px);. These imports are silently skipped.
suggestion: Extend the regex to optionally consume the media query portion after the URL.

message: Private method get_ccss_url() is defined but never called anywhere in the class. Dead code that could confuse future maintainers.
suggestion: Remove the unused method, or add a @todo docblock noting it is reserved for future use.

message: SKIP_DEFER_HANDLES constant is described as 'CSS handles to skip during deferral' but is used for both exact handle matching (defer_stylesheets line 930) and URL substring matching via strpos (generate line 390). The name is misleading.
suggestion: Rename to SKIP_DEFER_ITEMS and update the doc comment to clarify matching semantics.

message: ccss_regeneration_cron() calls Critical_CSS::regenerate_all() without a require_once safety guard. While the class is loaded by Main::includes() during bootstrap, the inconsistency could cause subtle failures if the execution context differs.
suggestion: Add a class_exists check before calling regenerate_all() for consistency with the REST endpoint pattern.

message: handleRegenerate calls await onRegenerate() without checking if onRegenerate is a function. If the component is rendered standalone without the prop, this throws a TypeError.
suggestion: Add a guard to check that onRegenerate is a function before calling it.

message: CCSS status is always fetched on mount regardless of whether the criticalCSS feature is enabled or which tab is active. This makes unnecessary API calls on every admin page load.
suggestion: Only call fetchCcssStatus if the file_optimisation.criticalCSS setting is true and activeTab is 'fileOptimization'.

message: get_sample_url('archive') calls setup_postdata() without verifying the setup was successful. If the post ID is invalid, get_the_time() operates on stale global $post state, potentially returning incorrect dates for the archive URL.
suggestion: Verify the post is valid before calling setup_postdata, or build the archive URL directly.
